title: SportsMemo Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: SportsMemo review, checked 20 Nov 2026: $7 single plays, all sales final, its leaderboard and expert runs checked, and 17 years of buyer posts.
dek: A pick marketplace founded in 2004 by Ted Sevransky, better known as Teddy Covers, and bought by WagerTalk in 2018. On 20 Nov 2026 every single play on its picks page was $7.00. Sales are final, nothing is guaranteed, and every record shown is published by the company that sells the picks. Buyer posts are few: a cluster of forum threads from 2009 and 2010 and two negative reviews from 2022.

short_answer: SportsMemo is a real, long running pick marketplace. The sportsmemo.com domain was registered on 24 Jul 2004, and saved copies of the site from 2006 show it selling plays from a group of named handicappers, led by its founder Ted Sevransky, who writes as Teddy Covers. WagerTalk announced it had bought SportsMemo on 20 Aug 2018. Today the terms give a Las Vegas address and Nevada law, and the refund page names Wager Talk Media, LP as the parent company. In that narrow sense the business is legitimate.

Whether its experts win is a different question. On 20 Nov 2026 the site showed a profit leaderboard and expert cards full of runs such as "35-20 (64%) FOOTBALL HEATER" and "13-8-0 since Oct 27, 2026." These numbers come from the seller. The Yesterday's Plays page sent us to a WagerTalk login, and we found no full, time stamped log of every pick that a buyer could check.

When we did the arithmetic on the seller's own figures, most percentages were correct for the windows shown, but the windows are chosen after the fact, one expert's 2024 NFL lines cannot both be true, another expert's run appeared in two versions on the same page, and the leaderboard's 7 day, 365 day and year to date tabs showed identical profit figures.

Prices are low per play, $7.00, which limits what a buyer can lose on the picks themselves. Independent buyer talk is thin and mostly old. Forum threads from 2009 and 2010 mix praise for the analysis with complaints about losing runs, lines that moved before members could bet, and records that were hard to find. Two CapperTek reviews from 2022 were negative. Treat the records as marketing, not proof, and log every play yourself.
pricing_intro: All rows were on sportsmemo.com/picks and the homepage on 20 Nov 2026. Three days earlier most single plays were $5.00; on 20 Nov every listed play was $7.00. Prices change daily as experts post new plays. For history: a saved copy from January 2006 shows full season packages at $999 to $1,299 and a newsletter at $59 to $179, and a saved copy from December 2016 shows single plays at $20 to $39, an all access autobill at $299 and full season passes from $399 to $899.

guarantee: SportsMemo offers no win guarantee. The FAQ answers "Are your picks guaranteed to win?" with "No picks or predictions are guaranteed." and adds that "past performance is not indicative of future results."

The refund page says purchases are made from "Wager Talk Media, LP", that "All Sales are Final and products are sold "as is".", and that "Once a product or service has been purchased, delivered, and/or viewed, no refunds will be issued." It also lists cases that never earn a refund, including in state team restrictions, lack of access to authorized sportsbooks and "Undelivered email or SMS notifications as we are unable to guarantee the deliverability". Card charges show as "WT/SM* PICKS AND PAR".

The terms say the buyer's exclusive remedy is "a refund of the price paid" or replacement of the product, at the company's option. The FAQ says a subscription can be cancelled at any time and access runs to the end of the billing period. It does not say whether subscriptions renew automatically.

This is a change from earlier years. In December 2016 single plays on the site were sold as "guaranteed to cash or" the handicapper's next top play "is on the house." We found no such wording on 20 Nov 2026. Losses on the bets themselves were never covered.

claims_note: How we checked: SportsMemo publishes expert cards, an experts page and a leaderboard with several period tabs. We read them on 20 Nov 2026, recomputed every win percentage from the wins and losses shown (pushes left out), and compared figures for the same expert across pages. We could not read the Yesterday's Plays page, which asks for a WagerTalk login, so we could not check any figure pick by pick.

Each blurb picks its own window: since 14 Nov, the last 45 days, since December 2025, since 2007, one past season. A window chosen after the fact tells you little, because every handicapper has a hot stretch somewhere. Where the page also showed a longer figure for the same expert, the longer figure was weaker.

The leaderboard ranks experts by dollar profit on a $100 bet size. Its header says "Win/Loss and Units", but the main table shows only profit. On 20 Nov 2026 the 7 day, 365 day and year to date tabs all showed the same top five with identical dollar figures, so we treat the board as a short term snapshot.

Several cards cite rankings on "P&P + W&W", meaning Picks and Parlays and Winners and Whiners. In August 2025 WagerTalk Media announced a partnership with both sites, so those rankings are not independent of SportsMemo.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every SportsMemo pick with the line, odds and release time, and no third party audit.

What the seller publishes: a profit leaderboard, expert cards and bios with selected runs, and a Yesterday's Plays page. When we opened Yesterday's Plays on 20 Nov 2026 it sent us to identity.wagertalk.com to log in, the same result as on 17 Nov.

Older figures exist only as forum posts. In September and November 2009 an account posting as SportsMemo on the Las Vegas Advisor forum listed yearly newsletter records and multi year records for two handicappers, for example 268-210 (56.1%) on football for one of them from 2006 to September 2009. Those are the seller's own numbers and we could not check them.

Background: the sportsmemo.com domain was registered on 24 Jul 2004. A saved copy from January 2006 describes it as a handicapping site with free picks, a forum and handicapper blogs, naming Ted Sevransky (Teddy Covers) and others. A saved copy from December 2016 carries the footer "SPORTSMEMO, INC, 1-800-575-3069". WagerTalk's August 2018 release names Sevransky as the founder and quotes WagerTalk co founders Marco D'Angelo and Lawrence Prezman. On 20 Nov 2026 Teddy Covers was still listed among SportsMemo's experts.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no SportsMemo pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how SportsMemo experts perform.
our_data.context: For scale: on the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer talk about SportsMemo is thin and mostly old. The fullest threads are on the Las Vegas Advisor forum from 2009 and 2010; the only recent buyer reviews we found are two on CapperTek from 2022. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Across 17 years we found buyer talk in only two places. Three Las Vegas Advisor forum threads from September 2009 to December 2010 hold most of it. There, members split: some praised the newsletter's game breakdowns and called two of its handicappers long term winners, while others tallied a 27 and 77 run over two Saturdays, said picks once differed between the email and the website, said they often could not bet at the release number, and described the site as a marketing operation that promotes whichever capper is hot while full records stay hard to find. The SportsMemo account answered with yearly winning totals that we could not check. The second place is CapperTek, where two 2022 reviews of SportsMemo were both negative, one questioning a handicapper's posted records and one saying a buyer lost their whole bankroll. CapperTek's 14 reviews of WagerTalk, the parent company, from 2021 to 2026 are almost all negative but none mentions SportsMemo. TheRX lists "Sports Memo Crew" write ups among content members should not post. We found nothing about SportsMemo on Reddit or the BBB. The pattern is old, small and mixed, with the same complaint about selective records repeating in 2010 and 2022.

A Las Vegas Advisor member tallied the site's plays over the two previous Saturdays at 27-77, down 65.6 units, and argued that few paid handicappers beat -110 lines long term. A well known bettor replying in the thread called two days a cherry picked sample, while agreeing that long term winners are rare.

In the same thread, one member wrote that he stopped using a SportsMemo handicapper after picks were flipped by accident, with sides differing between the email and the website. Another said he often could not bet at the release number, and a third argued that the site promotes winning runs while full records are hard to find.

On the second page of that thread, members agreed that services commonly feature the hot handicapper and bury overall records. One member posted 2010 football figures showing two SportsMemo handicappers took opposite approaches, one mostly underdogs and one mostly favorites, to explain why their results moved together. Another called SportsMemo a marketing operation that sells plays, and was asked by others to tone it down.

A thread opened by a member saying the SportsMemo best bets newsletter was down for the year drew mixed replies. One subscriber said the newsletter broke down games well but counted his own results at 56-52, down 1.2 units. Another was harsh about its NHL picks.

An account posting as SportsMemo replied in that thread that the newsletter was only slightly down for the football season and listed winning yearly totals for 2007 to 2009. It also gave its NHL writer's record as 20-24, down 10.15 units, and said the newsletter cost about $3.50 an issue. These are the seller's figures.

In a thread about one SportsMemo handicapper, members split. One called him and another SportsMemo handicapper lifetime winners while warning that the second had some very poor years; another member said he saw no evidence either could hit 54% long term. The SportsMemo account posted multi year records in reply.

A CapperTek reviewer wrote that one SportsMemo handicapper always seemed to be 9 and 1 or 8 and 2 over his last 10 picks, asked where those picks were tracked, and said that after buying picks and comparing them with what the site posted, they concluded the records were not genuine. No amount lost is given.

Another CapperTek reviewer said they had tried many SportsMemo handicappers and found them all poor, singled out the same handicapper for confident write ups, and said they lost their entire bankroll. They advised others to avoid the service. No dollar figure is given.

CapperTek lists 14 reviews of WagerTalk, which owns SportsMemo. Thirteen with text are negative, describing losing purchases, records the reviewers found misleading and, in one case, reward points they could not use. None of them names SportsMemo, so they describe the parent company's own storefront, not this one.

TheRX service play guidelines, posted in March 2023, list "Sports Memo Crew" under write ups members should not post, and list all WagerTalk cappers under services not to post. The rules give no reason.

Reddit archive post searches for sportsmemo in r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting returned no posts, and our saved copy of ten betting subreddits from 2024 to 2026 had no mention of SportsMemo. Web searches found no SportsMemo thread on Sportsbook Review, TheRX or Covers. A BBB search for sportsmemo found no business profile. We did not read review sites that block automated reading.

conflicts: The leaderboard, the expert records and the Yesterday's Plays page are all run by the company that sells the picks. None is an independent audit.

SportsMemo is owned by Wager Talk Media, LP, which also runs WagerTalk. The refund page says card charges show as "WT/SM* PICKS AND PAR." WagerTalk's 2018 release quotes Marco D'Angelo as a WagerTalk co founder, and he also sells picks on WagerTalk.

Several expert cards cite rankings on Picks and Parlays and Winners and Whiners. WagerTalk Media announced a partnership with both sites in August 2025, so those rankings come from inside the same network.
TheRX, an independent forum, asks members not to post SportsMemo write ups or any WagerTalk capper's plays, which limits outside tracking of these experts.
strengths: A named parent company, a Las Vegas address and written terms under Nevada law.
A long history: the domain dates to 2004, saved copies show the business selling plays in 2006 and 2016, and its founder is still listed among its experts.
Low entry prices: every single play was $7.00 on 20 Nov 2026, so trying one expert costs little.
Prices are shown before you buy, and the FAQ says a subscription can be cancelled at any time with access to the end of the period.
Most percentages on the expert cards are arithmetically correct for the windows shown.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a streak, a ranking or a short leaderboard chosen and published by the seller, and the Yesterday's Plays page needs a login.

Some figures do not hold together: one expert's two 2024 NFL lines cannot both be true, another expert's run appeared in two versions on the same day, and three leaderboard periods showed identical numbers.
All sales are final and nothing is guaranteed; the 2016 style next play free guarantee is gone.
Many prices are shown against a higher regular price, which pushes quick decisions.
Buyer complaints repeat across years: picks differing between email and website and lines moving before buyers could bet (2010), and records buyers did not trust (2010 and 2022).
Rankings cited from partner sites come from inside the same business network.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the expert's last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Compare the headline run with any longer figure for the same expert on the same page; on SportsMemo the longer figure was usually weaker.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Check whether you can still get the release line. A pick that only wins at the original number is worth less to you.
Remember that all sales are final; buy single plays before any multi day pass.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business founded in 2004, owned since 2018 by WagerTalk, with a named parent company, a Las Vegas address and written terms. We could not verify that its experts win over time, because the site does not publish a full, time stamped record of every pick, and we found no court or regulator action involving it.

Wager Talk Media, LP, the company behind WagerTalk, is named on the refund page as the parent company. WagerTalk announced the purchase on 20 Aug 2018. The site was founded by Ted Sevransky, who writes as Teddy Covers.

On 20 Nov 2026 every single play on the picks page was $7.00, one shown next to a $25.00 regular price. No multi day passes were listed that day; on 17 Nov two experts had 3 day passes at $49. Prices change daily.
Does SportsMemo offer refunds or a guarantee?

No. The FAQ says no picks are guaranteed, and the refund policy says all sales are final and no refunds are issued once a product is delivered or viewed. Undelivered emails or texts do not earn a refund either.
Does SportsMemo have a verified record?

No. The site shows a profit leaderboard and selected runs in each expert's card, all published by SportsMemo. Some of those figures did not agree with each other on the same day, and we found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

At $7 a play the price of the picks is small, but sales are final and nothing is guaranteed. What is unproven is whether any expert beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and nothing covers your betting losses.
